patterns.pattern: Nomenclature-phenotype mismatch where a nominal hallmark (facial dysmorphism) is subtle, non-penetrant, and non-diagnostic across cohorts.
patterns.abstraction: Syndromic disorder classifications often enshrine physical signs in diagnostic entity names that lack discriminating power, creating clinical search bias.
patterns.instance: In the Sleyp et al. (2022) cohort of 14 patients with NEDSFBA, no individual facial dysmorphic feature exceeded 70% penetrance, and craniofacial phenotypes lacked a recognizable gestalt to enable computational or visual diagnosis without sequencing.
patterns.direction: Quantitative facial anthropometry and high-density deep-learning morphometrics calibrated against phenotypically overlapping intellectual disability cohorts.
patterns.support: Strong across multiple findings (F3, F4, F8) documenting subtle, heterogeneous dysmorphic features across 14 individuals.
sources: Sleyp et al. (2022) De novo missense variants in the E3 ubiquitin ligase adaptor KLHL20 cause a developmental disorder with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and autism spectrum disorder PMID:36214804
Sleyp et al. (2022) MOLECULAR DIAGNOSTICS IN AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER: NEXT GENERATION SEQUENCING AND FACIAL PHENOTYPING IN MEDICAL GENETICS https://lirias.kuleuven.be/handle/20.500.12942/703598
patterns.hypothesis: Automated facial recognition tools classify KLHL20 patients with no higher accuracy than non-syndromic autism cohorts due to the absence of a distinct facial gestalt.
patterns.novelty: Counterintuitive given OMIM nomenclature explicitly incorporating 'facial dysmorphism' into the disease definition.

patterns.pattern: Biphasic natural history characterized by early infantile paroxysmal seizures evolving into persistent behavioral and intellectual impairments.
patterns.abstraction: Age-dependent symptom transition from acute paroxysmal neurological crises in infancy to stable neurobehavioral morbidity in late childhood and adulthood.
patterns.instance: Infantile spasms and early-onset seizures predominate in the first years of life (reported in Kuroda et al. (2024) and Sleyp et al. (2022)), but seizure penetrance remains incomplete (<80%), while developmental delay and autism spectrum/hyperactivity persist into later stages.
patterns.direction: Longitudinal natural history studies tracking seizure remission rates and adulthood neuropsychiatric trajectories in KLHL20 cohorts.
patterns.support: Strong support from F1, F5, and F6 documenting 100% penetrance of intellectual disability versus incomplete, age-concentrated seizure penetrance.
sources: Sleyp et al. (2022) De novo missense variants in the E3 ubiquitin ligase adaptor KLHL20 cause a developmental disorder with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and autism spectrum disorder PMID:36214804
Kuroda et al. (2024) Early-onset West syndrome with developmental delay associated with a novel KLHL20 variant 10.1002/ajmg.a.63600
patterns.hypothesis: Early-onset epilepsy in KLHL20-related disorder undergoes spontaneous or treatment-associated remission in adolescence without parallel mitigation of behavioral disturbances.
patterns.novelty: Differentiates KLHL20 disorder from relentlessly progressive neurodegenerative developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.

patterns.pattern: Exclusionary systemic findings delineate KLHL20 from overlapping developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
patterns.abstraction: Diagnostic discrimination in non-specific encephalopathy syndromes relies as much on negative findings as on positive phenotypic features.
patterns.instance: KLHL20-related disease lacks neurovisceral storage signs, obligatory structural cardiac anomalies, rapid neurodegenerative lethality, and limb-reduction deficiencies (F2), separating it from metabolic and syndromic DEEs.
patterns.direction: Systematic codification of negative/exclusionary phenopackets into automated clinical decision support algorithms for rare epileptic encephalopathies.
patterns.support: Moderate-to-strong support documented in discovery cohort evaluations and differential diagnoses (F2, F8).
sources: Sleyp et al. (2022) De novo missense variants in the E3 ubiquitin ligase adaptor KLHL20 cause a developmental disorder with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and autism spectrum disorder PMID:36214804
Kuroda et al. (2024) Early-onset West syndrome with developmental delay associated with a novel KLHL20 variant 10.1002/ajmg.a.63600
patterns.hypothesis: Patients exhibiting structural cardiac defects or rapid motor decline carry secondary pathogenic variants or alternative syndromic diagnoses rather than isolated KLHL20 missense mutations.
patterns.novelty: Clinical differential diagnosis focuses heavily on positive markers, often neglecting defined negative boundary criteria.

patterns.pattern: Domain-restricted mutational clustering in Kelch beta-propeller without sub-domain genotype-phenotype divergence.
patterns.abstraction: Pathogenic variation restricted to a single interaction domain yields homogenous clinical expressivity despite hotspot versus non-hotspot distribution.
patterns.instance: All 14 reported patients in the index cohort carry de novo missense variants in the Kelch domain, with 11/14 sharing the recurrent p.Gly357Arg allele; however, seizure semiology and developmental severity do not significantly differ between hotspot and non-hotspot missense carriers.
patterns.direction: Biochemical and structural characterization of KLHL20 Kelch domain variants to assess whether substrate binding affinity correlates with clinical severity.
patterns.support: High concordance across cohort analyses and curation evaluations (F6, F7, F9, F14, F16).
sources: Sleyp et al. (2022) De novo missense variants in the E3 ubiquitin ligase adaptor KLHL20 cause a developmental disorder with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and autism spectrum disorder PMID:36214804
ClinGen (n.d.) Autosomal dominant by ClinGen submission information facts https://thegencc.org/submissions/SGC-107240.1
patterns.hypothesis: The recurrence of p.Gly357Arg reflects hypermutable CpG dinucleotide kinetics rather than functional divergence from other Kelch propeller substrate-interface missense variants.
patterns.novelty: Challenges the assumption that recurrent disease hotspots inevitably confer distinct, more severe clinical phenotypes than adjacent domain variants.
